questions.stem: Loss of contractibility of myocyte occurs after the ischemic duration of-
questions.solutionHtml:
2 min
  • Loss of contractility: < 2 min


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 545

questions.stem: In an ischemic event, irreversible injury of myocyte occurs, first in which zone:
questions.solutionHtml:
Subendocardium
  • Irreversible injury of ischemic myocytes first occurs in the subendocardial zone. This region is especially susceptible to ischemia because:
  1. It is the last area to receive blood delivered by the epicardial vessels.
  2. Because it is exposed to relatively high intramural pressures, which act to impede the inflow of blood.
  3. Endocardium is perfused by being directly in contact with blood present in the ventricles, making the subendocardium more susceptible than the endocardium.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 545-547

questions.stem: The area of Myocyte necrosis can be identified by immersion of tissue flies in a solution of triphenyl tetrazolium chloride which provides a color of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Unstained
  • Pale unstained zone represents the infarcted myocardium.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 547, 548

questions.stem: At what duration of myocardial infarction does light microscopy demonstrate myocyte necrosis, hypereosinophilia, contraction band necrosis, and early neutrophil infiltrate:
questions.solutionHtml:
12-24hr
  • At 12-24 hr, light microscopy demonstrates
  • Ongoing coagulative necrosis, pyknosis of nuclei; myocyte hypereosinophilia; marginal contraction band necrosis; early neutrophilic infiltrate.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 547

questions.stem: At what duration of myocardial infarction light microscopy demonstrate new blood vessel and collagen depositions:
questions.solutionHtml:
10-14 days
  • At 10-14 days, light microscopy demonstrates well-established granulation tissue with new blood vessels and collagen deposition.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 547

questions.stem: Earliest light microscopic change in myocardial infarction is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Waviness of fiber
  • Earliest light microscopic change in myocardial infarction is the Waviness of fiber

Microscopic features of myocardial infarction and its repair. (A) One-day-old infarct showing coagulative necrosis and wavy fibers (elongated and narrow, as compared with adjacent standard fibers at right).




Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 547-549

questions.stem: Sublethal ischemic change which reflects the intracellular accumulation of salt and water in sarcoplasmic reticulum within known as:
questions.solutionHtml:
Myocytolysis
  • Sublethal ischemic change may be seen in the margins of infarcts: this so-called Myocyte Vacuolization or Myocytolysis reflects intracellular accumulations of salt and water within the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and marks myocytes that are viable but poorly contractile.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 547-549

questions.stem: In myocardial reperfusion injury, the maximum effect is caused by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Free radicals
  • Reperfusion injury may be mediated by oxidative stress, calcium overload, and inflammatory cells recruited after tissue reperfusion.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 549

questions.stem: Stunned myocardium term is related to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Biochemical abnormalities
  • Biochemical abnormalities (and their functional consequences) may also persist for days to weeks in reperfused myocytes. Such changes are thought to underlie a phenomenon referred to as stunned myocardium, a state of prolonged cardiac failure induced by short-term ischemia that usually recovers after several days.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 549, 550

questions.stem: At what duration Troponin T & I begin to rise in the blood vessel after myocardial infarction:
questions.solutionHtml:
3-12 hr
  • Troponins I and T are normally not detectable in circulation. Following an MI, levels of both begin to rise at 2-4 hours, thus we go for the closest Option: as the answer i.e. 3-12 hrs.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 550, 551

questions.stem: Earliest change in systemic hypertensive heart disease:

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in transverse the diameter of myocyte

questions.answerText: Increase in transverse the diameter of myocyte
questions.solutionHtml:
Increase in transverse the diameter of myocyte
  • Microscopically, the earliest change of systemic Hypertensive Heart Disease (HHD) is an increase in the transverse diameter of myocytes, which may be difficult to appreciate on routine microscopy.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 555, 556
